tasks.short: Pick theme activities, prepare materials, lead circle and small-group activities and routines, and note each child's progress.

steps.what: Preschool teacher picks the week's theme activities from the programme binder
Preschool teacher prepares cards, games and craft materials
Preschool teacher leads circle time on colour, shape, number and letter recognition
Preschool teacher guides hygiene routines, tidying and social skills during play
Preschool teacher ticks children's progress on paper observation lists

tasks.design: Theme activities sit in a shared library in {DOCS} tagged with the development goals, so the week plan is picked rather than copied. Observations are ticked on a tablet against the same goals in the student information system ({OTHER}); teaching and routines stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme binders and paper observation lists were copied and retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch pupil records systems track learning goals, and tablets are common in early-years classes.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching young children is hands-on and relational; observation is the teacher's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a song or a game into the moment a child gets it.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less paper around the day.

reach.learn: Whether shared activity cards help assistants lead groups alone.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil records system keeps pupil records and learning-goal tracking with a parent app.
Parents and staff have consent rights on pupil-data rules and tools that can monitor staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning the week to observations recorded; reporting to parents is outside.
Input contract: development goals list in the student information system set by the school; activity library kept by the early-years team; fallback is paper.
Teaching and routines do not change.
No child data goes into any outside tool.
unknowns: Whether the school uses tablets in early years.
research_questions: Do tablet observations make progress talks with parents easier?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Teachers who already record observations digitally save only on planning.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree group rules and routines, make picture cards, practise rules with the children, redirect behaviour, note incidents and tell parents.

steps.what: Preschool teacher agrees group rules and routines with colleagues
Preschool teacher draws and laminates picture cards for rules and the daily rhythm
Preschool teacher explains and practises procedures for maintaining order with the children
Preschool teacher enforces rules for behavior and redirects children through the day
Preschool teacher writes repeated incidents on a paper note for colleagues
Preschool teacher tells parents about the day at pick-up

tasks.design: Picture cards are printed from a shared template set in {DOCS} instead of drawn each year, and repeated incidents are noted with a short code and text in the student information system ({OTHER}) so colleagues on other days see them. Rules, redirection and the talk with parents stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cards were hand-made and incident notes were on paper that colleagues did not see.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems have note types colleagues can read, and template sets are easy to share.
tasks.still_hard: Order in a preschool group comes from routine and relationship, not records.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a group of four-year-olds with a look and a song.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; colleagues share what they see.

reach.task: Handle behaviour on days the teacher is away
reach.learn: Whether shared incident notes keep responses consistent.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil records system keeps pupil records and a parent app.
Inferring pupils' emotions with AI is banned; this design uses no AI.
Parents have consent rights on pupil-data rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from agreeing rules to telling parents; formal support plans are outside.
Input contract: incident codes agreed in the school's pupil-data rules; template set kept by the early-years team; fallback is paper.
Practice, redirection and pick-up talks do not change.
Parent time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: How many teachers share the group per week.
Number of incidents noted per week.
research_questions: Do shared notes make responses to behaviour more consistent across the week?

incremental.description: Preschool teacher learns the incident codes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Groups with one teacher all week share little and save little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe which children need support or challenge, check progress per goal, adapt activities and word materials, and update the group plan.

steps.what: Preschool teacher observes which children need extra support or challenge
Preschool teacher compares observation lists with the development goals on paper
Preschool teacher adapts teaching methods: simpler steps, more language, more challenge
Preschool teacher makes picture-word materials in the home languages of children's families

loop.input: The theme's key words and short parent tips chosen by the teacher, and the target home language.
loop.output: Picture-word cards and a short tip sheet in that language.
loop.check: Only the teacher's key words appear; a back-translation into Dutch must match the meaning of each word and tip; a parent or colleague who speaks the language checks a new language once before the teacher uses it.
loop.stop: One translation and one retry per sheet; then the teacher uses the Dutch version with pictures.
loop.why_not_simpler: Translating tips in plain words for parents is language work; a fixed dictionary covers single words only.

steps.what: Preschool teacher works with small groups using the adapted activities
Preschool teacher writes the group plan with who gets what support

tasks.design: The student information system ({OTHER}) shows each child's observations against the development goals, and the group plan is generated from the groups the teacher sets. A bounded step translates the theme's key words and short parent tips into families' home languages, checked by back-translation and once by a speaker of the language; observing and adapting stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were on paper lists, and home-language materials depended on a parent who happened to help.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems track goals, and Dutch lesson editors already translate and rewrite text at another level.
tasks.still_hard: Translations of tips can sound wrong to parents; no child data may go into the tool.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a quiet child needs and finding the activity that draws them in.

ambition.what: Families who speak little Dutch who get home-language word cards for every theme.

tasks.altitude: The teacher checks translations and generated plans instead of making them by hand.

reach.learn: Whether the word cards are used at home.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
A Dutch pupil records system tracks learning goals per pupil.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets a child's level is high-risk; translating word cards does neither.

assumptions: Boundary: from observation to the group plan; formal support plans are outside.

Input contract: observations per goal recorded by teachers; key words chosen per theme by the teacher; first check of each new language by a parent or colleague who speaks it; fallback is Dutch cards with pictures.
No child names or data go into the translation step.
Observing, adapting and small-group work do not change.
unknowns: Number of home languages in the group.
Whether observations are recorded per goal today.
research_questions: Do home-language cards raise parents' use of theme words at home?

already_counted.description: Preschool teacher reviews translated cards and back-translations.
Preschool teacher reviews the progress-per-goal view.

incremental.description: Preschool teacher picks key words and tips per theme.
ICT coordinator handles tool approval and the privacy check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Groups where all families speak Dutch gain only from the progress view.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the child's progress, book parent talks, meet parents about progress and priorities, record agreements and send home tips.

steps.what: Preschool teacher gathers observations and progress for the child before the talk
Preschool teacher arranges talk times with parents by notes and messages
Preschool teacher meets parents to discuss progress, needs and their priorities
Preschool teacher writes agreements and home tips in the child file
Preschool teacher e-mails the agreed tips to the parents
Parents practise the tips with their child at home

tasks.design: A child summary is generated from the observations per goal in the student information system ({OTHER}) for the teacher to check before the talk, and parents pick a talk slot in the parent app. Agreements go into a short template in the child file, and once the teacher saves them the tips are sent to the parents through the app as written.
tasks.previous_blocker: Summaries were written from paper lists, and talk times were arranged one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems have parent apps and report templates fed by recorded goals.
tasks.still_hard: The talk itself is about trust; some parents do not use the app.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what parents worry about and agreeing one thing they can do at home.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; preparation and follow-up are lighter.

reach.task: Schedule parent evenings for the whole school
reach.learn: Whether self-booking slots end the paper rounds.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil records system keeps learning-goal tracking and a parent app.
Parents have consent rights on pupil-data rules.
Support needs recorded about a child can be health data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing the talk to tips sent; support plans are outside.
Input contract: observations per goal recorded by teachers; talk slots set by the teacher in the parent app; fallback is notes and paper lists.
Parent time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Share of parents using the parent app.
Number of parent talks per year.
research_questions: Do written home tips change what parents practise?

already_counted.description: Preschool teacher checks the generated child summary before the talk.

incremental.description: Preschool teacher sets talk slots in the app.

approvals.approved_version: Tips and agreements as saved by the teacher in s4; later edits send a correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Schools where few parents use the app keep arranging talks by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The preschool teacher keeps teaching, observing and talking with parents; paper lists, cards and arranging shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who reaches every family in their own language and spends prep time on play, not paper.
